options: proteins that bind to specific antigens
molecules on the surface of pathogens
questions.why: Antibodies are proteins with complementary shapes that bind to specific antigens.

questions.q: A patient has an infection caused by a virus. Why are antibiotics not prescribed?
options: Viruses are resistant to all drugs.
Antibiotics kill bacteria but do not affect viruses.
questions.why: Antibiotics treat bacterial infections only; using them unnecessarily also selects resistant bacteria.

questions.q: Why is a vaccinated person protected for many years?
options: The vaccine contains antibodies that stay in the blood for life.
The pathogen can no longer enter the body.
Memory cells quickly produce antibodies on later infection.
questions.why: Vaccination produces memory cells, giving long-term active immunity.

questions.q: Describe what is meant by a transmissible disease.
questions.model: A disease in which the pathogen can be passed from one host to another.
points: passed from one host to another
